stories.headline: Samsung and AMD sign MOU for HBM4 supply for Instinct MI455X GPUs and next-gen DDR5

key_facts.fact: On March 18, Samsung Electronics signed a Memorandum of Understanding with AMD to supply industry-leading HBM4 memory for AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs and next-generation DDR5 solutions for AMD EPYC processors and the AMD Helios platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics today announced it has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with AMD to expand their strategic collaboration on industry-leading HBM4 supply for AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs and next-generation DDR5 solutions for AMD EPYC processors and the AMD Helios platform.

key_facts.fact: The deal expands the existing Samsung-AMD relationship and positions Samsung as a key memory supplier for AMD's next-generation AI accelerators, competing with SK Hynix which supplies HBM to Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung will provide next-generation memory chips for AMD's future AI processors. Both companies are securing long-term agreements amid high AI chip demand.

key_facts.fact: The collaboration covers both high-bandwidth memory for AMD's GPU accelerators and standard server memory for AMD's CPU platforms, making it a comprehensive AI infrastructure partnership.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies will collaborate on industry-leading HBM4 supply for AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs and next-generation DDR5 solutions for AMD EPYC processors and the AMD Helios platform.

stories.headline: Samsung co-CEO declares 'unprecedented supercycle,' pursues 3-to-5-year chip contracts

key_facts.fact: At Samsung's annual shareholder meeting on March 18 in Suwon, co-CEO Jun Young-hyun said the chipmaker is working with major customers to shift to multi-year contracts of three-to-five years to shield them from potential demand fluctuations.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics co-CEO said the chipmaker is working with major customers to shift to multi-year contracts of three-to-five years to shield them from potential demand fluctuations.

key_facts.fact: Jun stated the chip industry is entering an 'unprecedented supercycle' driven by growing investment in AI data centres, but cautioned Samsung must prepare for 'various scenarios' amid concerns about overheating in AI infrastructure spending.
key_facts.excerpt: There are concerns regarding overheating in investment in AI infrastructure. Accordingly, we plan to continuously seize opportunities arising from the AI cycle while preparing for various scenarios with a cautious view.

key_facts.fact: Samsung shares rose 7.5% following the meeting and are up 62% since January 2026, with memory chip prices surging due to supply bottlenecks.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung shares rose 7.5% following the meeting, up 62% since January 2026. Jun acknowledged memory chip prices surging due to supply bottlenecks.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang praised Samsung's HBM4 chips at Nvidia's GTC conference and announced a foundry partnership with Samsung, narrowing the gap with rival SK Hynix in high-bandwidth memory development.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO Jensen Huang praised Samsung's HBM4 chips at Nvidia's GTC conference and announced a foundry partnership with the Korean firm, narrowing Samsung's gap with SK Hynix in high bandwidth memory chip development.

stories.headline: Chinese lab demonstrates controlling humanoid robots from orbit using OpenClaw and space-based LLMs

key_facts.fact: A joint lab of GuoXing Aerospace Technology and Shanghai Jiao Tong University successfully demonstrated remote, intelligent control of ground-based humanoid robots using OpenClaw and computing power from orbiting satellites, as reported by Xinhua on March 18.
key_facts.excerpt: In a milestone fusion of three frontier technologies, a Chinese lab has recently successfully demonstrated remote, intelligent control of ground-based humanoid robots using OpenClaw and computing power from orbit.

key_facts.fact: In the trial, an operator issued voice commands that OpenClaw uploaded to China's orbiting satellites; onboard large language models performed in-orbit inference, then transmitted decisions back to Earth for OpenClaw to control ground robot movements.
key_facts.excerpt: In the trial, the operator issued voice commands that OpenClaw uploaded to China's orbiting satellites. Onboard large language models performed in-orbit inference using space computing power, then transmitted decisions back to Earth for OpenClaw to control ground robot movements.

key_facts.fact: In January, GuoXing Aerospace uplinked Alibaba's Qwen3 large language model to its space-based computing center, enabling end-to-end AI inference from orbit using its 12-satellite constellation launched in May.
key_facts.excerpt: In January, GuoXing Aerospace, a commercial aerospace firm, uplinked Alibaba's Qwen3 large language model to its space-based computing center, enabling end-to-end AI inference from orbit.

key_facts.fact: GuoXing plans to deploy 2,800 specialized computing satellites by 2035, with second and third clusters launching in 2026 and a 1,000-satellite network operational by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: GuoXing plans to deploy 2,800 specialized computing satellites by 2035, with second and third clusters launching in 2026 and a 1,000-satellite network operational by 2030.

stories.headline: Taiwan's Techman Robot unveils Nvidia-powered wheeled humanoid for smart factories at GTC 2026

key_facts.fact: Taiwan-based Techman Robot introduced its TM Xplore I next-generation humanoid robot at NVIDIA GTC 2026 on March 18, developed jointly with Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT) and NVIDIA.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan robot Techman Robot introduced its next-generation humanoid robot, TM Xplore I, at the Nvidia GPU Technology Conference (GTC) 2026 in San Jose, marking a joint development effort with Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT) and Nvidia on March 18.

key_facts.fact: The platform features a humanoid upper body mounted on a wheeled mobile base powered by Nvidia's Jetson Thor module for high-performance edge AI computing, with Vision-Language-Action (VLA) capabilities for processing visual and linguistic inputs.
key_facts.excerpt: The TM Xplore I platform features a humanoid upper body mounted on a wheeled mobile base... powered by Nvidia's Jetson Thor module, enabling high-performance edge AI computing.

key_facts.fact: The robot targets precision industries including semiconductor manufacturing, electronics assembly, and automotive production, and can quickly adapt to new tasks without extensive reprogramming.
key_facts.excerpt: The robot combines mobility with manual dexterity, making it suitable for precision industries including semiconductor manufacturing, electronics assembly, and automotive production.

key_facts.fact: Techman aims to commercialize its wheeled humanoid robots and file patents within the year, following a strategy called 'See, Think, Act — Powered by AI Robotics' using NVIDIA's Isaac Sim for simulation before real-world deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: Techman aims to commercialize its wheeled humanoid robots and file patents within the year.

stories.headline: Swarmer, Ukraine-tested drone autonomy software company, surges 520% on Nasdaq debut

key_facts.fact: Swarmer Inc. (Nasdaq: SWMR), an AI drone autonomy software company with systems deployed in over 100,000 combat missions in Ukraine since April 2024, closed its IPO on March 18, selling 3.45 million shares at $5 each for net proceeds of approximately $14.7 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The Austin-based artificial intelligence drone software company raised $15 million by selling 3 million shares at $5 each, initially valuing the business at just over $60 million.

key_facts.fact: Shares surged as much as 700% intraday before closing up 520% at $31 on day one, making it one of the strongest US listings since Newsmax's IPO a year ago. On day two they rose another 77% to close at $55.
key_facts.excerpt: Swarmer shares soared 77% to finish at $55 on Wednesday, piling onto Tuesday's explosive Nasdaq debut. The drone-autonomy software outfit had already rocketed 520% above its $5 IPO price on day one.

key_facts.fact: Backed by Erik Prince, Swarmer operates as a vendor-agnostic software provider rather than a drone manufacturer, with a platform designed to coordinate nearly 700 drones simultaneously. CEO Alex Fink told Reuters the Nasdaq listing aimed to build a public defense-tech brand.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's miltech startup Swarmer develops software systems that allow unmanned vehicles to act autonomously and work together in large swarms.

key_facts.fact: The company reported revenue of only $309,920 for 2025, a 6% decline from the prior year, with a net loss of approximately $8.5 million, more than four times deeper than in 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Swarmer reported revenue of $309,920 for the year ended December 31, 2025, representing a roughly 6% decline from the prior year, while its net loss widened to about $8.5 million.

stories.headline: Ondas and Heidelberg form ONBERG joint venture for autonomous drone defense in Europe

key_facts.fact: On March 18, Ondas Inc. (Nasdaq: ONDS) and Heidelberger Druckmaschinen AG formed ONBERG Autonomous Systems, a joint venture to deliver autonomous drone defense and security systems across Germany and Ukraine in its first phase.
key_facts.excerpt: Ondas Inc. and Heidelberger Druckmaschinen AG today announced the formation of ONBERG Autonomous Systems, a joint venture... to deliver autonomous drone defense and security systems across Germany and Ukraine in first phase.

key_facts.fact: ONBERG combines Ondas Autonomous Systems' battle-proven counter-UAS, ISR, and autonomous security technologies (including the Iron Drone Raider) with Heidelberg's 175 years of German industrial manufacturing capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: The joint venture will combine OAS' battle-proven counter-UAS, ISR, and autonomous security technologies with Heidelberg's 175 years of German engineering excellence, scalable industrial manufacturing capabilities.

key_facts.fact: The Brandenburg an der Havel production site in Germany will be expanded into a center of excellence for autonomous defense systems, featuring localized assembly and full production using European supply chains.
key_facts.excerpt: Including expansion of the Brandenburg an der Havel site into a center of excellence for autonomous defense systems.

key_facts.fact: The JV formalizes an MOU signed in December 2025 in the presence of German Federal Minister of Economics Katherina Reiche, and aims to become a European one-stop shop for autonomous drone defense protecting critical infrastructure, borders, and national security.
key_facts.excerpt: HD Advanced Technologies and Ondas Autonomous Systems establish joint venture for drone defense in Europe... implementing the Memorandum of Understanding signed in December 2025 in the presence of Federal Minister of Economics Katherina Reiche.

stories.headline: Rocket Lab secures record $190M contract for 20 hypersonic HASTE test flights

key_facts.fact: On March 18, Rocket Lab announced a $190 million contract from the US Department of War for 20 hypersonic test flights using its HASTE (Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron) rocket, the largest single launch contract in the company's history.
key_facts.excerpt: Rocket Lab has won a US$190 million contract from the United States Department of War for a series of hypersonic test flights using its HASTE launch vehicle. It is the largest single launch contract in the NZ-founded company's history.

key_facts.fact: The four-year agreement covers launches under the Multi-Service Advanced Capability Hypersonic Test Bed (MACH-TB) 2.0 programme, a partnership between the Department of War and the Naval Surface Warfare Centre Crane Division to accelerate hypersonic flight testing at speeds above Mach 5.
key_facts.excerpt: The four-year agreement covers 20 test flights of Rocket Lab's Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron (HASTE) rocket, a modified version of its Electron launcher designed to carry suborbital payloads of up to 700 kilograms at speeds above Mach 5.

key_facts.fact: The contract lifts Rocket Lab's total order backlog to more than $2 billion, with the company having sold 28 launches in Q1 2026 alone — nearly as many as it sold during all of 2025. Total launch backlog stands at 70 missions.
key_facts.excerpt: The contract takes Rocket Lab's launch backlog to 70 missions, and the company has sold 28 launches in the first quarter of 2026 — almost as many as it sold during the whole of 2025.

key_facts.fact: CEO Peter Beck said the expanded partnership will 'strengthen US national security by providing rapid and affordable hypersonic testing,' with the first HASTE launch under the new contract expected within months.
key_facts.excerpt: Our advanced technology, responsive launch schedules, and mass production of our HASTE hypersonic rockets are enabling faster progress across a range of hypersonic experiments by our government and industry partners.
